title: Create stress-tested FP8/INT8 quantization profiles and end-to-end ranking validation
creator: Lena Park
description: Deliver a set of validated FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles for the production reranker family (RERANK-v3) plus an automated calibration and accuracy-validation pipeline. Goals: (1) preserve ranking quality (NDCG@10 and MRR@10 within acceptance thresholds), (2) document per-layer quantization choices and fallback policies, (3) build reproducible calibration runs and gating for canary rollouts.
metrics_summary: Baseline (FP16): NDCG@10=0.742, MRR@10=0.651, p50 latency=38ms. FP8 candidate (per-channel weight, symmetric activations clipped at 99.999 percentile): NDCG@10=0.737 (-0.67%), MRR@10=0.649 (-0.31%), p50 latency=28ms (-26%). INT8 candidate (per-tensor weights, asymmetric activations, percentile clipping 99.995): NDCG@10=0.730 (-1.62%), MRR@10=0.643 (-1.23%), p50 latency=30ms (-21%). Note: FP8 shows the best cost/quality trade-off in initial runs; INT8 has larger regressions on long-tail queries.
decision: Adopt dual-profile strategy: promote the FP8-per-channel profile as default for RERANK-v3 in runtime-1.21, with an INT8-perf profile available as a lower-cost option behind an explicit route. Calibration method: activation clipping via percentile-based collection (99.999th for FP8, 99.995th for INT8), KL-based histogram refinement for problematic layers, per-channel weight quantization for FP8 and per-tensor for INT8 where layers are memory-bandwidth dominated. Canary gate: reject profile if NDCG@10 drops >0.8% or MRR@10 drops >0.6% on the primary validation set.
runbook: 1) Prepare calibration corpus: 12k labeled query-document pairs (mix of head/mid/tail). 2) Warm up model with representative traffic to collect activation ranges. 3) Run layer-wise histogram collection (256 bins) and compute percentiles. 4) Apply symmetric/per-channel scales for FP8, asymmetric/per-tensor for INT8. 5) Run quantized forward pass with simulated KV cache and full-ranking pipeline. 6) Compute NDCG@1/3/5/10 and MRR@10. 7) If regression above gate, perform KL histogram sweep on top-10 offending layers and re-run. 8) Produce artifacts: quantized checkpoint, profile.json, perf traces, evaluation report. 9) Upload to artifacts and open PR for rollout.
calibration_details: Calibration corpus size: 12k queries (4k head, 5k mid, 3k tail). Batch sampling: temperature-balanced by query length and top-k feature distribution. Range collection method: streaming min/max + histogram with exponential decay; prefer percentile clipping over naive min/max due to outliers. Weight quantization: per-channel symmetric for conv/linear kernels where observed per-channel ranges differ by >10x; otherwise per-tensor. Biases kept in FP16. KV cache simulated to include 32-512 token prefixes to surface activation scale shifts in long-sequence reranks.
experimental_notes:
- Observed consistent NDCG drop concentrated in queries with many near-duplicate candidates (high lexical similarity). Hypothesis: activation clipping compresses discrimination at shallow scorer layers. Tried KL tuning and increasing calibration corpus tail fraction; best gains when adding 20% more tail examples.
- INT8 regressions larger on attention projection layers; adding 4-bit fine-grained per-head scaling mitigated some loss but added engineering complexity.
- Throughput: quantized kernels reduce GPU memory bandwidth by ~18% for FP8 route, enabling ~1.3x increase in concurrent streams on the same Dedicated instance.
